confidence_rationale: Direct empirical demonstration that one drive (hunger) suppresses several others (thirst, anxiety, innate fear, social interaction), that the suppression is graded and context-conditional (often only when food is accessible), and that a hypothalamic node integrates internal state + external factors + anticipated yield. This is the multidrive-competition phenomenon MECH-394 asserts, measured at circuit + behavioural levels. Confidence held below 0.85 because the mapping is functional, not mechanistic -- REE has no AgRP/ARC analogue, and the paper shows hunger-over-others rather than a full N-axis arbitration policy.
failure_signatures: Hunger's dominance is context-gated: it suppresses competing drives 'often only when food is accessible', so a fixed drive hierarchy (hunger > thirst > fear) is wrong -- the ranking is conditional on affordance availability. A multidrive policy that ignores environmental affordance state would mispredict when a lower-ranked drive wins.

The paper establishes hunger-suppresses-others but does not characterise the reciprocal case (does extreme thirst or fear suppress hunger symmetrically?), so the competition geometry beyond the hunger-dominant regime is unconstrained by this evidence.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Hunger increases its capacity to suppress competing motivational systems (thirst, anxiety-related behaviour, innate fear, social interaction), often only when food is accessible; AgRP/ARC neurons integrate internal state, external factors, and anticipated yield, so behavioural choice under competing needs is a flexible computation rather than a fixed priority.
mapping.ree_translation: MECH-394 asserts that when several drive axes are simultaneously active, behaviour is selected by a soft-competitive orchestration over context, per-axis satiation, inter-drive competition, and developmental phase -- not a fixed priority or single-axis winner. Burnett et al. supply the biological existence proof: drive competition is real, the winning drive suppresses the others, and the suppression strength is modulated by satiation level (degree of hunger) and context (food accessibility) -- exactly the orchestration variables MECH-394 names. The ARC integration of internal state + external factors + anticipated yield is the biological instance of the contextual arbitration MECH-394 requires. Also grounds SD-060: thirst, fear, and social interaction are treated as first-class competing drive axes, not collapsed into a single scalar.
mapping.mapping_caveat: The paper demonstrates one drive (hunger) dominating others, not a symmetric N-axis arbitration policy; REE's MECH-394 generalises beyond the hunger-dominant case the data establish. The mapping is functional (competition + contextual gating) not mechanistic -- REE has no AgRP/arcuate substrate, so this evidences the computation MECH-394 posits, not its implementation. Mouse appetitive/defensive behaviour; transfer to REE's gridworld drive register assumes the contextual-competition principle is substrate-general.
mapping.source_context: In vivo mouse study: battery of behavioural assays (feeding vs thirst, anxiety, innate fear, social interaction) under food deprivation + real-time fibre-photometry monitoring of arcuate (ARC/AgRP) neuron activity, with optogenetic manipulation.

confidence_components.notes: Neuron, Krashes lab; converging behavioural battery + photometry + optogenetics. Mapping_fidelity high because the orchestration-over-context/satiation framing is almost verbatim what MECH-394 claims; capped below 0.8 by the hunger-dominant-only scope and absence of a REE arcuate analogue.
